newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India GDRs fall, outpaced by locals.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India GDRs fall, outpaced by locals.

text.p: Indian global depository receipts gave up ground on Wednesday, continuing a trend of underperformance against the local market, traders said.
The premium of GDR shares in the HSBC James Capel Indian index has fallen to 18.36 percent from 24.90 percent on July 2.

"GDRs are sentiment driven instruments and tend to run ahead of local markets. Investors have reacted emotionally to recent losses -- taking profits -- and clients are staying away with volume dominated by traders," a trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.08 points lower at 83.83, an 1.27 percent fall, with the premium over the local market at 18.36 percent from 18.50 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index shed 35.58 points to 4,185.64.
Reliance lost 50 cents to $21.25/$21.75 and Hindalco shed $1.50 to $31.00/$32.00.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index lost 1.03 points firmer, falling to 74.81 points, a premium of 43.59 percent over the local market.
Taiwan continued a strong run, traders said, with strong buying in electronics shares, which dominate Taiwanese GDRs.
"Valuations look expensive but there is such a weight of liquidity from local money that it is hard to argue," a trader said.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 2.66 points higher at 139.54, representing a discount to the local market of 2.33 percent.
